id: ZZTEST.KEY.01
title: The Missing Shul Key
grade: 3
kind: chapter
book: The Shul on Linden Street
chapter: 1
topic: Mysteries
source: original
---
Every Friday, Dovid helped his Zaidy open the little shul on Linden Street. Zaidy kept the big brass key on a red string. Dovid loved the heavy click it made in the lock.

This Friday, Zaidy patted his coat pocket. Then he patted the other one. His face grew puzzled. "Dovid," he said slowly, "I think the key is missing."
===
Dovid looked at the ground. He saw leaves, a bottle cap and a long trail of muddy paw prints. The prints led away from the shul door and around the corner.

"Zaidy, look!" Dovid said. "Someone was here before us. Someone with four feet."

Zaidy bent down and smiled a little. "A detective notices small things," he said. "What else do you see?"
===
Dovid followed the paw prints to the back steps. There, beside a flowerpot, sat Mrs. Levin's puppy, Biscuit. A red string hung from his mouth.

Dovid gasped. He could not believe his eyes. Biscuit wagged his tail as if he had done a great mitzvah.

"Biscuit found our key!" Dovid laughed. But when he looked closer, the red string was empty. The key was gone.
--- words
puzzled: not sure what is going on, and trying to figure it out
detective: a person who looks for clues to solve a mystery
trail: a line of marks that shows where someone went
gasped: took a quick, loud breath because of a surprise
